ai.title: Prompt hardening: JSON.stringify input, reordered context, structured
ai.summary: Prompt templates in backend/src/check-terminal-command.ts and backend/src/find-files/ now wrap user inputs in JSON.stringify instead of raw interpolation or backticks to prevent injection and delimiter confusion. Error handling in check-terminal-command.ts switches to structured logging with pino-style object passing and explicit message extraction. main-prompt.ts updates the file_updates system message to enforce stronger consideration of user modifications. Import order standardization applied across request-files-prompt.ts and check-new-files-necessary.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now treats your pasted text as plain data when deciding whether it looks like a terminal command or which files to open, instead of trusting the text to be safe. That means tricky punctuation or hidden markup in what you paste can no longer fool it into misreading your request. If you watched the logs you might also notice error messages now come with more structured detail, and the internal notes about past file changes now remind it to respect edits you've already made. Your experience stays the same today, but the system is now quietly better at keeping your input from being misinterpreted.

ai.title: Logger adds chunking for large payloads
ai.summary: Backend logger wraps pino to split oversized JSON payloads into chunks under 100k chars. Handles nested arrays and objects via recursive `splitData`. Extends `LoggerContext` with `fingerprintId`, `clientRequestId`, `messageId`. WebSocket middleware normalizes `discordId` to `undefined`.

eli5.text: The backend system that records activity logs can now split oversized messages into smaller pieces before saving them, instead of failing or truncating when something tries to log a very large chunk of data. Previously, extremely big payloads could overwhelm the logging process; now, payloads are broken into segments under a certain size limit and reassembled when needed. This change affects all internal logging across the platform, so if you were experiencing dropped or incomplete logs from large operations, those gaps should be reduced or eliminated.

ai.title: Remove debug logs from logger splitData
ai.summary: Removed two temporary console.log statements from `backend/src/util/logger.ts`. These logs were inside `splitData` and `splitAndLog`, used for debugging data chunking. This cleans up the backend logging utility.

eli5.text: If you looked at the backend's logging system today, you'd no longer see extra diagnostic messages cluttering the logs when large data chunks are being processed. The system still splits up bulky information for logging, but it quietly does so without printing intermediate debugging details to the console. This cleanup only affects the internal operations of the assistant's backend logging utility.

ai.title: Logger Tolerance Increased to 2000
ai.summary: The `TOLERANCE` constant in `backend/src/util/logger.ts` increased from 1000 to 2000. This expands the buffer for log context to prevent truncation of larger payloads. Internal change; no user-facing impact.

eli5.text: Internal logging system's buffer for message details doubled, letting it keep more context around logged events without cutting off larger entries. This is backend maintenance only, so you won't see anything different in the app. The change is live today, but its effect is purely internal.

ai.title: Adjust recursive chunk length in logger splitData
ai.summary: Recursive calls in `splitData` now subtract delimiter lengths (`','` for arrays, `{"${key}":},` for objects) from `characterLimit`. This prevents chunks from exceeding the limit when delimiters are added during serialization. Internal change to `backend/src/util/logger.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system breaks up very large log entries into smaller pieces, it now leaves a little extra room for the commas and labels it adds while splitting. This keeps each piece from accidentally running over the size limit when those joiners get tacked on. It only affects how the internal logging system packages big data before storing it, so you would not notice anything different day to day.

ai.title: CLI shutdown logs killed background processes
ai.summary: Moved background process termination logic in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to execute after credit summary logging. Added explicit console output for each killed process command and formatted error reporting for failed kills using `yellow` and `red` utilities. This change affects only the CLI exit sequence, ensuring process cleanup visibility occurs immediately before the final 'Codebuff out!' message.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task and prepares to close, it now tells you which of your helper programs it is stopping and shows an error if any fail to stop, before showing the final goodbye message. Previously, it silently killed these programs during shutdown. This is the kind of thing you would notice only if you started helper programs alongside the assistant and then watched it close, it mainly makes an already-quiet cleanup step slightly more visible.

ai.title: Increase logger chunk buffer to 5000
ai.summary: Renamed TOLERANCE to BUFFER and increased value from 2000 to 5000 in backend/src/util/logger.ts. Adjusts availableDataLimit calculation in splitAndLog to reserve more space for context before chunking. Internal logging utility change affecting backend only.

eli5.text: The backend logging system now saves a bigger chunk of context before splitting large messages, reserving 5,000 units of space instead of the previous 2,000. This affects only internal server-side logging and not what subscribers see in the app. You wouldn't notice any difference in your experience, as this change keeps server logs more readable and intact behind the scenes.

ai.title: Move process kill logging before summary output in CLI
ai.summary: Relocated the `backgroundProcesses` kill loop in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to execute before the credit summary and final exit message. This ensures 'Killed process' logs appear before the aggregated output during shutdown. Internal refactor; no functional change to process termination logic.

eli5.text: When you close the program, you will now see messages about which background tasks were stopped appearing before the summary of how much you used it, instead of after. The program still stops those background tasks the same way; only the order of the log messages on your screen changed. This is a behind-the-scenes tweak to make the shutdown output easier to read.

ai.title: Logger: fix chunk overflow, string split
ai.summary: Fixes logging chunk overflow in `backend/src/util/logger.ts`. Reduces context `BUFFER` 5000 to 1000; corrects recursive split budget to account for `[],` delimiter; adds dedicated string chunker using `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse` to avoid breaking escape sequences. Internal backend logging only.

eli5.text: Large log entries written to the backend's internal audit trail were occasionally being cut off mid-way through an item, which corrupted the record. The system now reserves a smaller safety margin for surrounding text when deciding where to split a log entry, and long strings of text are now broken at safe boundaries so quotes and special characters stay intact. These changes only affect the internal logging infrastructure and are already live.

ai.title: Add experimental cost mode for Gemini 2.5 Pro
ai.summary: Introduced `experimental` cost mode to the `CostMode` type and CLI options, routing agent operations to `streamGemini25ProWithFallbacks` instead of the previous `max` mode behavior. The `--experimental` flag is added to `npm-app` with a magenta greeting message, while `max` now defaults to standard high-quality models. Documentation in `what-models.mdx` updated to describe the new mode's use of cutting-edge features and potential instability.

eli5.text: If you start CodeBuff with a new --experimental flag, the program will briefly show a magenta message saying experimental mode is on, and then route your coding tasks through Gemini 2.5 Pro instead of the usual high-quality models. This new option is added alongside the existing --max and --lite choices, giving you a third way to pick how capable versus costly your session should be. The documentation has been updated to describe the trade-off: you get access to the newest models and features, but they may be less stable than the standard options.

This release bundles the latest improvements to prompt handling and logging, and adds experimental support for Google's new Gemini 2.5 Pro model. The version number itself only labels the release, which is now available to anyone installing or updating the tool.

eli5.text: When you are working on your own computer, the system now skips the special log-splitting and formatting step and just writes logs directly instead. This means your local development logs stay simple and easy to read, while logs from the live servers still go through the full custom processing for consistency. The change is already in place and only affects the internal tooling used during development.

ai.title: Send background process output to backend
ai.summary: Background process stdout/stderr now sent to backend via new `background_process_updates` tool results. `getBackgroundProcessUpdates` in `background-process-manager.ts` slices new output since last report, formats it, and appends to `lastToolResults` in `client.ts` before sending prompts. `terminal.ts` refactored: `formatResult` includes command, `getBackgroundProcessInfoString` moved to manager, `exitCode` removed from `BackgroundProcessInfo`. Covers npm-app core, client, and terminal utils; limits output to 5000 chars per stream.

eli5.text: The assistant can now see what's happening in programs that keep running in the background (like a long download or server). When you run a background task and then ask another question, the conversation now includes any output that task produced since the last message, so you don't have to check a separate terminal window. The new information is capped at 5,000 characters per stream to avoid overwhelming the chat.

ai.title: Truncate background process stderr from start
ai.summary: Refactored `truncateStringWithMessage` in `common/src/util/string.ts` to accept an options object with a `truncate` direction. `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` now truncates background process `stderr` from the start to preserve recent error context. `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` updated to use the new signature.

eli5.text: When a background task (like a program running behind the scenes) produces an error message that's too long, the system now cuts off the beginning of that message and keeps the end - where the most recent error details usually are. This means if you're checking on a background process that failed, you'll see the final error reason rather than the earlier parts of a long, scrolling log. Previously, it would cut off the end and keep the start, which often dropped the actual failure point.
